one_line_contribution: A measurement study that replaces write-time credit signals for agent-memory admission with per-item leave-one-out utility estimated inside the deployed top-k bundle and averaged over the item's retrieval neighborhood, and then asks whether that screen survives its own estimation noise by splitting projected-minus-realized gain into a winner's-curse term and an item-interference term.
closest_prior_work: Two lines, and the proposal under-argues against both. (1) Leave-one-out / influence / Shapley valuation of in-context examples: Nguyen and Wong 2023 is cited, but the broader data-valuation line (Data Shapley and LOO-influence data selection) already establishes per-example marginal utility estimated by ablation, plus the standard finding that such estimates are dominated by variance at small sample sizes. The proposal's differentiator is that utility is conditioned on the retrieval neighborhood and measured inside the deployed bundle, which reads as a deployment-distribution implementation detail of the same estimator rather than a new estimand; the mixed-effects item x neighborhood decomposition (E2/P2) is the only place it becomes a distinct claim, and P2's item-level threshold (25 percent sign flips, 30 percent of explained variance) is not calibrated against what pure sampling noise would produce at m ~ 6 binary paired observations per split, where sign flips near 50 percent are the null expectation. (2) Memory curation from downstream signal: Memory-R1-style RL memory managers, ReasoningBank, Agent Workflow Memory, Mem0/A-MEM/Memento. The proposal names these and matches compute on one of them, which is the right move. Separately, the statistical apparatus is textbook: winner's curse and shrinkage corrections for selection on noisy estimates are standard in model/hyperparameter selection (Cawley and Talbot on selection overfitting) and in bias correction for adaptively collected data (best-arm identification bias). So the contribution is the application target, not the machinery, and that is a 5-level novelty at best.
strongest_objection: The load-bearing decomposition in E3/P4 is not identified as written. G_unbiased is defined as the sum over retained items of the split-half utility u_i^(B), and these u_i are, by the proposal's own central argument, quantities defined only relative to the specific bundle B(q) they were measured in. But the EB-screened cell (cell 4) is evaluated at k=7 over a SMALLER bank, so for every probe query the deleted items are replaced by items that were originally ranked 8, 9, 10... and were therefore never in any probed bundle and never had their utility estimated at all. Screening here is not deletion, it is substitution with unmeasured items. Consequently G_unbiased - G_actual is a garbage-can residual that mixes (i) genuine item-item interference, (ii) the utility of promoted, never-probed items, (iii) probe-to-heldout retrieval shift, and (iv) the failure of additivity of LOO effects even among retained items. P4's refutation branch ("non-additivity dominates and is stable in m, therefore interference is the mechanism") cannot be reached from this design, because (ii) and (iii) do not shrink in m either. The second, compounding objection is estimator degeneracy: the outcome is string-matched EM, so each of the ~11.7 observations per item is a paired binary difference in {-1,0,+1}, and at pilot-level discordance rates the expected number of NON-ZERO observations per item per split half is well under one. The majority of items will have u_i^(A) exactly 0, the naive rule "keep if u_i > 0" will be decided by one or two lucky flips, and split-half correlation will be near zero. In that regime G_insample - G_unbiased is close to 100 percent of the projected gain by construction, so P4's headline prediction (>=40 percent winner's curse) is confirmed whether or not any utility signal exists, and the design cannot separate "utility exists but is noisily measured" from "utility is not measurable at this budget, so the entire admission criterion is vacuous." A pre-registered prediction that is true under its own null is not a test.
what_would_fix_it: Four concrete changes, in priority order. (1) Fix the projection so it applies to the bundle that is actually injected: either hold bundle composition constant under screening (drop an item and leave the slot empty or filled with a neutral placeholder, so no rank-8+ unprobed item is promoted), or re-probe the retained bank's post-screen bundles and define G_unbiased on those. Without this, the non-additivity residual is uninterpretable and P4 should not be the headline. (2) Report, before running, the expected number of discordant (non-zero) LOO observations per item at the pilot's flip rate, and if it is below roughly 2 per split half, switch the utility outcome to a continuous score (F1, or token-level/logprob margin on the gold answer) or raise m; the current design spends 3,200 episodes to produce mostly exact zeros. (3) Add an oracle-screen ceiling cell: fit the keep/drop rule directly on the held-out set (deliberately cheating) and evaluate end-to-end. If the oracle ceiling is below the pre-registered 3.5-point claim threshold, the entire 12-cell end-to-end grid is known in advance to be undecidable and the budget should be reallocated to the item-level analyses; this cell costs 1,000 episodes and is the single highest-information run in the plan. (4) Execute the literature search. The proposal's own admission that no search was performed means novelty is unestablished at submission time, and the pre-emptive retargeting argument is a hedge, not a clearance. Separately: E5 is contingent on P3 clearing 3.5 points (if EB-vs-no-memory lands at +2 under instruction A, "the advantage survives under B" has no advantage to survive), which is the same unestimable-contrast defect the proposal used to justify cutting the GEPA arm; either restructure E5 as an item-level rank-correlation-only analysis or cut it. Also, a 95th percentile cannot be estimated from 3 null replicates, so the stated noise-floor rule needs a parametric or permutation formulation.
missing_baseline: A randomized-bundle regression (or Shapley-style) attribution estimator at matched EPISODE budget. The LOO design burns 8 runs per probe query to get 7 observations; a design that samples one random 7-item bundle per query and runs it once buys 3,200 distinct queries instead of 400, then regresses the episode outcome on the bundle membership indicator matrix to recover per-item marginal utilities. This is the standard way to de-confound shared episode-level credit, it is far stronger than the Thompson-sampling curator the proposal uses as its RL straw competitor (baseline 8, which credits reward to all 7 co-injected items and will obviously lose), and at equal cost it may well have LOWER per-item variance than paired LOO despite being unpaired. Since the paper's premise is that paired counterfactual estimation is the right estimator and that the winner's curse is large at realistic budgets, an estimator that trades pairing for 8x more queries is exactly the comparison that decides the premise, and it is absent. Ablation (d), which recomputes unpaired differences on the SAME LOO runs, does not substitute for it because it holds the query count fixed. A secondary omission: no oracle/cheating screen to establish the achievable ceiling.
preprint_collision: The check is not thin, it is empty, and the proposal says so: two consecutive rounds of tooling failure, zero queries executed, zero titles or dates retrieved, and an explicit statement that the proposal has not been cleared against the last twelve months of arXiv. The honesty is creditable and the refusal to fabricate a CLOSEST/GAP table is the right call, but per the standard that an unsearched novelty claim is a weakness rather than a neutral, this is a direct hit on the novelty score and on the verdict. I cannot verify dates either, but the risk surface the proposal itself lists is exactly where a 2025-2026 preprint is most likely to sit: utility-based or reward-based memory pruning in the Memory-R1 / ReasoningBank / Mem0 / A-MEM / Memento cluster, and LOO/influence/Shapley valuation of in-context demonstrations. The proposal's fallback argument -- that a colliding preprint would leave the winner's-curse decomposition intact as a qualifying methods contribution -- only holds if that decomposition is sound, and per my strongest objection it currently is not, so the collision hedge is load-bearing on a component that itself needs repair. Given that the committed pre-submission search protocol is described but not executed, novelty here is asserted, not established, and a reviewer is entitled to treat it as unresolved.
